newsitem.title: INDIA: India November wheat, rice stocks 21.14 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India November wheat, rice stocks 21.14 mln tonnes.

text.p: India's wheat and rice stock were 21.14 million tonnes as of November 1, the Food Ministry said on Monday.
The ministry said in a statement that stocks held by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) were increasing, but it did not give details.
As of October 1, wheat and rice stocks totalled 19.7 million tonnes, well above the buffer norm set by the government of 16.6 million.
But the stocks were down sharply from 29.9 million tonnes in October 1995.
The statement said wheat stocks totalled 9.54 million tonnes as of November 1 and 10.36 million as of October 1.
"The stocks of wheat in the central pool are adequate to meet the full requirement of the public distribution system and government sponsored welfare schemes," the statement said.
Traders said a fall in government reserves had prompted caused wheat prices to rise in recent months by about 20 percent compared with prices a year ago.
The Food Ministry has expressed the hope that even if wheat procurement in the 1996/97 (July/June) season falls, it would still be possible to have reserves near prescribed levels on April 1, 1997.
The government has set a lower limit of 14.5 million tonnes of foodgrains, including 3.7 million tonnes of wheat and 10.8 million tonnes of rice, for April 1.
Government wheat procurement in the 1995/96 growing season dropped sharply to 8.2 million tonnes from 12.3 million the previous year due to a three million tonne shortfall in output.
